description:
Code, canonical tables and published figures for the paper Measurability of Baseball Pitching Biomechanics From a Single 2D View.

Each 3D pitch of the Driveline OpenBiomechanics Project is projected to a virtual camera swept over 24 azimuths and 7 elevations, giving 168 viewpoints. At every viewpoint a 2D estimator measures a quantity and is scored against that pitch's own 3D ground truth, after a leave-one-pitcher-out correction. The result is a graded measurability map over quantity and viewpoint: of the 42 kinematic columns evaluated, 30 reach at least one graded viewpoint and 12 reach none, and 1,151 of the 5,040 cells the retained rows span are graded.

Included are the projection, the estimators, the grading protocol, the scripts behind every table and figure of the paper, the frozen population identifiers with their checksum, and the row-by-row specification of all 42 estimators. The OpenBiomechanics recordings themselves are not redistributed; they are that project's public release and are cited rather than copied. The identifiers and checksum let the same 394 pitches by 98 pitchers be pulled from the original.

Code is released under the MIT Licence, the derived tables and figures under CC BY 4.0.
